title: Lynwood Pharma inference - call bullets & integration notes
content:
Raw call notes (11/12/2025) - Lynwood Pharmaceuticals / Technical intake
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood infra), Harper (Lynwood infra lead), Maya (Lynwood data privacy), Ravi (Lynwood ML lead)

Purpose: quick intake to scope Private deploy vs Dedicated + data residency / HIPAA constraints. Keep as capture — many open Qs.

High-level customer ask
- Deploy a conversational assistant that can ingest case reports and EHR snippets to surface suggested follow-ups and policy text.
- Must satisfy HIPAA + corporate retention rules; prefer VPC private-control-plane or on-prem package; will evaluate dedicated hosted if control plane encryption + certs meet security.

Key constraints and notes
- Data locality: all patient-identifiable data must remain in AWS account X (us-east-2). No tokenized secrets allowed back to hosted control plane unless explicit S3 lifecycle + audit are in place.
- KMS/HSM: Lynwood requires customer-managed CMKs in AWS KMS and HSM-backed key for signing. Need clear KMS integration path with Redwood Private.
- Audit & retention: 7 years retention policy for logs associated with investigational drug trials. Need configurable retention per-route; must support export to their Splunk.
- Network: Strict egress rules; only allow outbound to approved registries and Redwood image repo. On-prem option must be air-gapped friendly (OCI tarball).
- Compliance: SOC2 + HIPAA BAAs required. Legal said BAA is possible but need security questionnaire (we provided partial already).

Performance and infra expectations
- Peak queries: 55 req/sec burst, steady-state 18 req/sec. Typical prompt sizes 600-1,200 tokens, response averages 150-350 tokens.
- Latency goal: p95 <= 600ms for single-turn response (note: they prefer sub-500ms for UI snappiness). Acceptable fallback to 1.2s if cached answer hits.
- Throughput: plan for batching where possible; but UI needs some low-latency single-request paths.
- Preferred hw: Lynwood asked about H100 vs A10G cost tradeoffs. We should present estimated $/k token for both on dedicated pools and on-prem.

Model and quality considerations
- Model family: they are leaning to a smaller finetuned open model (<=30B) for cost + auditability. Also want to explore 13B quantized 8-bit baseline for low-latency UI flows.
- Hallucination risk: high sensitivity. Need eval harness with domain-specific prompt set (we should seed with 120 test prompts from their clinical QA docs).
- Explainability: they want per-token provenance/traceability to source documents (pointer to snippet + doc id). We'll need to map provenance data to our tracing hooks and surface via the app.

Operational gotchas called out by Lynwood
- KV cache invalidation: clinical KBs update weekly; must support targeted cache invalidation when a doc is updated.
- Canary rollout: they require multi-week canaries with traffic shadowing (no responses to users) before enabling production.
- Token accounting: they want per-route cost telemetry accessible to their finance team; must export token usage to their internal billing pipeline.
- Encryption in transit: besides TLS they require mutual TLS for control plane ops (we need to confirm Redwood Private supports mTLS).

Action items (owners + rough ETA)
- Diego: produce two infra proposals (Dedicated GPU pool cost estimate for A10G/H100 + Private VPC architecture diagram with KMS flows). ETA: 11/21/2025.
- Sofia: draft onramp checklist & prompt-eval template (seed with 120 clinical QA prompts). ETA: 11/19/2025 (first pass).
- Maya (Lynwood): share sample redacted clinical snippets (10-20 examples) and their retention policy doc. ETA: 11/14/2025.
- Harper (Lynwood): confirm outbound egress whitelist and whether we can use their internal image registry or must use Redwood images. ETA: 11/18/2025.
- Ravi (Lynwood): nominate product owner for goals + acceptance criteria for hallucination threshold. ETA: 11/17/2025.
- Legal sync: Redwood Legal to send full BAA + security questionnaire to Maya. (Sofia to escalate).

Open questions we must resolve (priority ordering)
1) Can we support customer-managed CMKs + HSM-backed signing for model artifacts and logs in their AWS account? If not, what mitigations (encryption-at-rest with envelope keys) will satisfy them?
2) Does Redwood Private support mTLS for the control plane today, or is it engineering work (est effort)?
3) For provenance traces we may need to persist doc ids with tokens — what is the cost impact on storage and on tokenization? Need rough numbers.
4) Is weekly KB invalidation sufficient or do they require per-document real-time reindexing for certain doc types (e.g., adverse events)?

Technical notes for internal follow-up
- Batching: suggest two-path runtime config: low-latency path (batch size 1–4, prefer int8 quantization, no KV prefetch) and bulk summarization path (batch size up to 32, async, higher quality fp16).
- KV cache: implement TTL + manual invalidation API tied to webhook from their CMS (we should propose a small webhook receiver in Private manifest).
- Quantization: recommend 4-bit/8-bit experiments for 13B. Provide benchmarks for p50/p95 latencies on A10G vs H100 for 1k token contexts. Diego to run microbenchmarks.
- Tracing: use Redwood Console tracing hooks and add a minimal provenance envelope per response (doc_id:span:start:end). Must ensure envelope stripping for PI redaction paths.

Meeting artifacts to attach to JIRA RINF-3124 (already created)
- This notes doc, initial infra sketches, prompt-eval seed (Sofia), sample redacted snippets (from customer when available)

Immediate next steps (this week)
- Sofia: email Harper/Maya with high-level Private vs Dedicated comparison table + any redwood requirement for CMK/HSM. (Today)
- Diego: schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive with Lynwood infra to walk through VPC peering and outbound rules. (By 11/17)
- Legal: route BAA draft to customer (Sofia to ping Legal).

Notes to self: keep this doc informal. Capture any slack snippet or quick thread that contains acceptance criteria. When we get the sample snippets, build initial evals in the hosted sandbox before trying private onboarding — cheaper and faster for prompt tuning.

End of capture.
